title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the fetus. However, choosing iron-rich and folate-rich foods can be a challenge. In this article, we'll introduce three recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for pregnant women to get the necessary nutrients.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients during pregnancy. Iron helps prevent anemia, while folate supports the development of the baby's brain and nervous system. Vitamin C also plays a vital role in enhancing iron absorption. Here are three recipes that combine iron with vitamin C:

* Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl with Orange
 + 100g grilled chicken (20g protein, 1.5mg iron)
 + 100g mixed vegetables (20mg vitamin C, 1mg iron)
 + 1 orange (100mg vitamin C)
* Recipe 2: Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry with Bell Peppers
 + 100g beef stir-fry (25g protein, 2mg iron)
 + 100g mixed vegetables (20mg vitamin C, 1mg iron)
 + 1 bell pepper (100mg vitamin C)
* Recipe 3: Grilled Fish and Salad Bowl with Lemon
 + 100g grilled fish (20g protein, 1mg iron)
 + 100g mixed greens (20mg vitamin C, 1mg iron)
 + 1 lemon (100mg vitamin C)

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's essential to be mindful of food safety to avoid any risks to health. Here are some notes:

* Choose fresh and safe ingredients
* Cook food thoroughly before eating
* Avoid eating raw or undercooked food
* Wash hands before preparing and eating food

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips to help pregnant women get enough iron and folate:

* Eat a variety of foods to ensure adequate nutrient intake
* Take prenatal vitamins as directed by a healthcare provider
* Consult a [meal planner](/planner) for a balanced diet
* Explore the [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) for more information on pregnancy nutrition

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about pregnancy nutrition, they should seek help from a healthcare provider or registered dietitian. They can provide personalized advice and guidance to ensure a healthy pregnancy.

## Explore on Pregnancy Meal Planner

Use these Pregnancy Meal Planner pages next — each link goes to a different part of the site:

- [iron-focused pregnancy meal plan](/planner?health=anemia&goal=increase_iron_calcium_protein)
- [pregnancy meal plan articles](/blog/thuc-don-ba-bau)
- [pregnancy nutrition blog](/blog)
- [Pregnancy Meal Planner Premium](/premium)

## Sources
The information in this article is based on reliable sources, including the [WHO](https://www.who.int/tools/elena/interventions/nutrition-counselling-pregnancy) and [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/people-at-risk/pregnant-women.html).
